QuestionText: Which of the following is a NAMING word (Noun)?
Explanation: 'School' is a noun — it is the name of a place. 'Run' is an action, 'Happy' is a describing word, 'Quickly' tells how something is done.

QuestionText: Which of the following is a NAMING word (Noun)?
Explanation: 'Flower' is a noun — the name of a thing. 'Jump' is an action, 'Fast' and 'Beautiful' are describing words.

QuestionText: Which of the following is a NAMING word (Noun)?
Explanation: 'Dog' is a noun — the name of an animal. 'Eat' and 'Run' are action words, 'Big' is a describing word.

QuestionText: Which of the following is a NAMING word (Noun)?
Explanation: 'Table' is a noun — the name of a thing in your home. 'Dance' is an action, 'Tall' and 'Quick' are describing words.

QuestionText: Which of the following is a NAMING word (Noun)?
Explanation: 'City' is a noun — the name of a place. 'Fly' and 'Swim' are actions, 'Large' is a describing word.

QuestionText: Which of the following is a NAMING word (Noun)?
Explanation: 'Book' is a noun — the name of a thing. 'Read' and 'Write' are actions, 'Small' is a describing word.

QuestionText: Which of the following is a NAMING word (Noun)?
Explanation: 'River' is a noun — the name of a natural place. 'Flow' is an action, 'Blue' and 'Fast' are describing words.

QuestionText: Which of the following is a NAMING word (Noun)?
Explanation: 'Teacher' is a noun — the name of a person. 'Teach' is an action, 'Kind' is a describing word.

QuestionText: Which of the following is a NAMING word (Noun)?
Explanation: 'Bicycle' is a noun — the name of a vehicle with two wheels. 'Ride' is an action, 'Fast' and 'Quickly' describe speed.

QuestionText: Which of the following is a NAMING word (Noun)?
Explanation: 'Pen' is a noun — the name of a thing you use to write. 'Write' is an action, 'Blue' and 'Small' are describing words.

QuestionText: Which of the following is a NAMING word (Noun)?
Explanation: 'Mango' is a noun — the name of a fruit. 'Eat' and 'Peel' are actions, 'Sweet' is a describing word.

QuestionText: Which of the following is a NAMING word (Noun)?
Explanation: 'Hospital' is a noun — the name of a place where sick people are treated. 'Sick' and 'Helpful' are describing words.

QuestionText: Which of the following is a NAMING word (Noun)?
Explanation: 'Mountain' is a noun — the name of a very tall landform. 'Climb' is an action, 'Tall' and 'Slowly' are describing words.

QuestionText: What is the FEMININE of 'King'?
Explanation: The feminine of 'King' is 'Queen'. A King is a male ruler, and a Queen is a female ruler of a kingdom!

QuestionText: What is the MASCULINE of 'Hen'?
Explanation: The masculine of 'Hen' is 'Cock' (also called a Rooster). A Hen is a female chicken and a Cock is a male chicken!

QuestionText: What is the FEMININE of 'Boy'?
Explanation: The feminine of 'Boy' is 'Girl'. A boy grows up to be a man, and a girl grows up to be a woman!

QuestionText: What is the FEMININE of 'Father'?
Explanation: The feminine of 'Father' is 'Mother'. Every family has a father and a mother!

QuestionText: What is the FEMININE of 'Brother'?
Explanation: The feminine of 'Brother' is 'Sister'. A brother is a male sibling and a sister is a female sibling!

QuestionText: What is the FEMININE of 'Lion'?
Explanation: The feminine of 'Lion' is 'Lioness'. Female lions are called lionesses and they are excellent hunters!

QuestionText: What is the FEMININE of 'Uncle'?
Explanation: The feminine of 'Uncle' is 'Aunt'. Your father's or mother's brother is your Uncle, and their sister is your Aunt!

QuestionText: What is the FEMININE of 'Grandfather'?
Explanation: The feminine of 'Grandfather' is 'Grandmother'. Your grandparents are your grandfather and grandmother!

QuestionText: What is the MASCULINE of 'Cow'?
Explanation: The masculine of 'Cow' is 'Bull'. A Cow is the female and a Bull is the male of the same animal!

QuestionText: What is the MASCULINE of 'Duck'?
Explanation: The masculine of 'Duck' is 'Drake'. A female duck is just called a duck, but the male is called a drake!

QuestionText: What is the FEMININE of 'Tiger'?
Explanation: The feminine of 'Tiger' is 'Tigress'. The female tiger is called a tigress and she takes care of her cubs!

QuestionText: What is the MASCULINE of 'Mare'? (A mare is a female horse)
Explanation: The masculine of 'Mare' (female horse) is 'Stallion' (male horse). A foal is a baby horse!

QuestionText: What is the PLURAL of 'Cat'?
Explanation: The plural of 'Cat' is 'Cats'. We add 's' to make most words plural. One Cat → Two Cats!

QuestionText: What is the PLURAL of 'Box'?
Explanation: The plural of 'Box' is 'Boxes'. Words ending in 'x' get 'es' added. One Box → Two Boxes!

QuestionText: What is the PLURAL of 'Dog'?
Explanation: The plural of 'Dog' is 'Dogs'. We simply add 's'. One Dog → Two Dogs!

QuestionText: What is the PLURAL of 'Bus'?
Explanation: The plural of 'Bus' is 'Buses'. Words ending in 's' get 'es' added. One Bus → Two Buses!

QuestionText: What is the PLURAL of 'Baby'?
Explanation: The plural of 'Baby' is 'Babies'. When a word ends in 'y' after a consonant, we change 'y' to 'ies'. One Baby → Two Babies!

QuestionText: What is the PLURAL of 'Tree'?
Explanation: The plural of 'Tree' is 'Trees'. We simply add 's'. One Tree → Two Trees!

QuestionText: What is the PLURAL of 'Church'?
Explanation: The plural of 'Church' is 'Churches'. Words ending in 'ch' get 'es' added. One Church → Two Churches!

QuestionText: What is the PLURAL of 'Leaf'?
Explanation: The plural of 'Leaf' is 'Leaves'. Words ending in 'f' often change to 'ves'. One Leaf → Many Leaves!

QuestionText: What is the PLURAL of 'Mango'?
Explanation: The plural of 'Mango' is 'Mangoes'. Words ending in 'o' often get 'es' added. One Mango → Two Mangoes!

QuestionText: What is the PLURAL of 'Wish'?
Explanation: The plural of 'Wish' is 'Wishes'. Words ending in 'sh' get 'es' added. One Wish → Three Wishes (like in a fairy tale)!

QuestionText: What is the PLURAL of 'Fox'?
Explanation: The plural of 'Fox' is 'Foxes'. Words ending in 'x' get 'es' added. One Fox → Two Foxes!

QuestionText: What is the PLURAL of 'Star'?
Explanation: The plural of 'Star' is 'Stars'. We simply add 's'. One Star → A sky full of Stars!

QuestionText: What is the PLURAL of 'Fly'?
Explanation: The plural of 'Fly' is 'Flies'. When a word ends in 'y' after a consonant, change 'y' to 'ies'. One Fly → Many Flies!

QuestionText: Tom is my friend. ___ is very kind. Which word fills the blank?
Explanation: We use 'He' when talking about a boy or man. Tom is a boy, so we say 'He is very kind.'

QuestionText: My sister and I went to school. ___ were very happy. Which word fills the blank?
Explanation: 'We' is used when talking about yourself and someone else. 'My sister and I' means two people including yourself, so we use 'We'.

QuestionText: The dog is in the garden. ___ is eating a bone. Which word fills the blank?
Explanation: 'It' is used for animals or things (when we don't specify male or female). The dog is an animal, so we use 'It'.

QuestionText: Lisa and Tom are good friends. ___ play together every day. Which word fills the blank?
Explanation: 'They' is used for more than one person. Lisa and Tom are two people, so we use 'They'.

QuestionText: I have a red ball. ___ is very bouncy. Which word fills the blank?
Explanation: 'It' is used for things. A ball is a thing, so we say 'It is very bouncy.'

QuestionText: My mother is a doctor. ___ works in a hospital. Which word fills the blank?
Explanation: 'She' is used for a woman or girl. Mother is a woman, so we say 'She works in a hospital.'

QuestionText: My father is tall. ___ plays cricket with me every evening. Which word fills the blank?
Explanation: 'He' is used for a man or boy. Father is a man, so we say 'He plays cricket.'

QuestionText: The flowers in the vase are fresh. ___ are very beautiful. Which word fills the blank?
Explanation: 'They' is used for more than one thing. Flowers (plural) are things, so we use 'They are very beautiful.'

QuestionText: Riya and I are going to the park. ___ will play there for an hour. Which word fills the blank?
Explanation: 'We' is used when you and someone else do something together. 'Riya and I' includes yourself, so we use 'We'.

QuestionText: My cat is named Whiskers. ___ has soft white fur. Which word fills the blank?
Explanation: 'It' is used for animals when we don't specify male or female. The cat is an animal, so we use 'It'.

QuestionText: My grandparents are visiting us next week. ___ will come by train. Which word fills the blank?
Explanation: 'They' is used for more than one person. Grandparents means two people, so we use 'They'.

QuestionText: The sun shines in the sky. ___ gives us light and warmth every day. Which word fills the blank?
Explanation: 'It' is used for things. The sun is a thing in the sky, so we say 'It gives us light and warmth.'
